Cimanīcarita
or Cīmanīcarita. kāvya; a love poem based on a contemporary scandal in the harem of a Muslim Nobleman Allāh Vardi-Khan Turkman of Shah Jehan's Court (1606-1660); composed in 1656 A. D. by Nīlakaṇṭha Śukla, son of Janārdana Śukla an. Hīrā (daughter of Vacchācārya) an. pupil of Bhaṭṭoji Dīkṣita.
B. II. 132. Bikaner 3017. (d. 1670). BORI. 357 of 1884-87. (d. 1688). 698 (i) of 1886-92 (d. 1744). BORI. D. XIII. i. 269. 270. Peters. [Page064-b] IV. p. 26 (no. 698 (i)). Extr. p. 23. Rgb. 357. Udaipur II. 174, 16.
Q. in Sabhyālam3karaṇa of Govindajit. See P. K. Gode, Stud. in Ind. Lit. His.. III. p.. 129-131. On the historical background of the kāvya see P. K. Gode, Poona Ori. VI. iii & iv. p.. 149-158; see also. ABORI. IX. p.. 331-2 an. NIA. V. p.. 177-183.
Ed. N. A. Gore, J. of Ori. Studies, M. S. Uni. Baroda, I. i. (1950).

Cimanīśataka
Q. by Govindajit in Sabhyālam3karaṇa. Same a. Cimanīcarita; see above.

Cīmanarāmaśarman
--Gayāditīrthaśrāddha.
Pt.. Benares, 1919. See IO. Pt.. Bk.. 1938, p.. 658. 896.
